headline: Tabled equity plan vote, adopted AI guidelines, approved consent agenda and out-of-district requests
summary: The Waltham School Committee met in executive session on collective bargaining and litigation matters, then held a regular meeting covering curriculum updates, an equity plan presentation, and an AI guidance policy. The Committee approved the consent agenda, staff out-of-district requests, AI guidelines, and bills on the warrant, while tabling a vote on the three-year equity plan until September 2, 2026.
decisions: Voted to move to Executive Session for collective bargaining and litigation strategy discussions, returning to the regular meeting at 6:00 pm.
Voted to move agenda items 6, 7 and 8 out of order.
Approved the Consent Agenda, including minutes, retirements, and resignations.
Approved the staff out of district requests for the 2026-2027 school year.
Voted to hear from off-committee members regarding the Anti-Racism, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion plan.
Tabled the Anti-Racism, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion three-year plan until the September 2, 2026 meeting.
Voted to have the Curriculum and Instruction highlight presentation posted to the district and all school websites.
Adopted the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Guidelines as presented.
Voted to pay the bills on the warrant.

 McCarthy.  Mayor McCarthy presided.

 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs.  Coleman, to move agenda

 Waltham High School parent Nicole Piche-Nicholas informed the members that a 
 survey about the WHS schedule was shared with WPS families, students and alumni. 
 An overview of the results indicated families valued providing feedback before the 
 final proposal stage, data and evidence, and the majority of respondents preferred 
 keeping an eight block schedule. 
 There were no students present at the meeting.

 Dr. Mendonsa provided a brief overview of the equity plan process which began with 
 the equity audit.  The plan encompasses the vision that Waltham Public Schools is “A 
 district where every student is known, valued, and supported to achieve at the 
 highest levels.”. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mr.  Tarallo, to hear from 
 off-committee members.  All in favor. 
 Ms. Jackie Herrera explained the two important pillars that were the focus of the plan 
 process: Instruction and Student Experience and Adult Learning and Development. 
 She provided the key themes stemming from the audit results.  Ms. Paula Mendoza 
 shared the plan whereby students should be able to experience affirming, 
 high-expectation learning environments, staff should feel well-equipped and 
 supported, and the district should be able to close persistent opportunity gaps during 
 the next three years. 
 Dr. Nadene Stein reviewed the recommendations from each of the priority pillars. 
 Year one of the plan (this upcoming school year) will focus on building a strong 
 foundation.  Year two will include piloting, building and refining models, capacity and 
 processes.  The final year will see district-wide implementation, student-led 
 programming, and institutionalizing equitable practices. 
 Dr. Mendonsa shared the plan for this year, how success will be measured and the 
 governance and accountability.  Ms. Haybi Garcia highlighted how the work and 
 progress will be communicated to the community throughout the three year process. 
 The superintendent requested the School Committee approve the three year plan as 
 the district’s guiding equity framework, and participate in the process. 
 Multiple questions were asked by School Committee members and the 
 superintendent and Assistant Superintendent of Curriculum and Instruction 
 responded.  It was noted that a shared definition of “equity” be considered an 
 important priority. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mrs. Coleman, seconded by Mr.  Tarallo, to table this matter 
 until the September 2, 2026 meeting.  All in favor. 
 Assistant Superintendent for Curriculum and Instruction Dr. Shannon Conley shared 
 an overview from each department from the 2025-2026 school year.  DIBELS data 
 shows that, at the elementary level, there is an increase in the number of students 
 who are meeting or exceeding grade level benchmarks.  At the secondary level, 
 iReady results show an increase in the number of students meeting or exceeding 
 grade level benchmarks.  Dr. Conley provided AP Language and AP Literature exam 
 scores. 
 Highlights from the Fine and Performing Arts Department, AP exam scores as well as 
 plans for the upcoming school year were shared.  Achievements and updates were

 The superintendent reminded the Committee that the first day of school for students 
 in grades 1-12 is Wednesday, September 2nd and the first day for Pre-K and 
 Kindergarten students is Thursday, September 10th.  She also advised online 
 registration is available for students looking to play a fall sport and tryouts begin the 
 week of August 24th. 
 Dr. Mendonsa reviewed the year relative to her three evaluation goals and four DESE 
 standards.  She completed year two of the New Superintendent Induction Program 
 (NSIP), worked on the development of the three year district equity plan, and 
 assisted with the plans for future programming at 617 Lexington Street.  She shared 
 progress made and goals for the upcoming year within the areas of instructional 
 leadership, management and operations, family and community engagement, and 
 professional culture.  Dr. Mendonsa reviewed what the year, through its ups and 
 downs, has taught her and then her self-evaluation. 
 Nothing new was shared in this area.
